value.rationale: The two counts are canonical connected four-vertex induced graphlets used in motif statistics, so their covariance and correlation have direct natural meaning. The degree-three projection overlap vanishes at p=1/2 despite nonzero individual leading n^5 variances, exposing a truly second-order n^4 covariance from three distinct support sizes. Their competition yields a nontrivial asymmetric pair of n^-1 density sign crossings, unlike routine first-order motif covariance laws or a known graphlet table. The exact all-n moment formula and sharp microscopic sign structure can benchmark rare dependence effects in finite-network motif analysis; no unsupported joint CLT or full-density classification is claimed.

final_claim: For G(n,p), n>=4, the mixed induced-claw K1,3 versus induced-path P4 covariance has the explicit 3-support polynomial in RESULT.md; at p=1/2+lambda/n, n^-4 Cov tends to (12lambda^2-8lambda-1)/2048 with exactly two local zero branches (2±sqrt7)/(6n)+1/2+O(n^-2); n*Corr tends to sqrt(3)/4 times the same quadratic.
limitations: No claim of complete all-density covariance zero classification, joint independence or new general subgraph factor theory.
The first roots are local in any fixed compact n(p-1/2) interval containing both simple roots; outside this window unexamined.
The 1990 and 1979 older full papers were not accessible; explicit priority risk, without automatic O failure.
The finite checks do not themselves verify infinite n or asymptotic uniformity; analytical exact formulas and ordinary IFT do.
No external Lean/expert attestation; existing independent audit was not performed before this review.
